rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maḥill is the place or time of arrival; here the offering's slaughter place is the Ḥaram, all of which follows the Kaʿba, as 22:33 indicates.
rows.anchor: فمحل الدين وقت وجوب قضائه ومحل الهدي المكان الذي يحل فيه ذبحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All pilgrims—single, combining, enjoying, or performing ʿumra—may not shave before sacrificing their offering; an unprevented pilgrim does so at Mina.
rows.anchor: وهذا الحكم عام لجميع الحاج من المفرد والقارن والمتمتع والمعتمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Hajj, shaving is better than trimming; trimming a quarter of the head suffices, though shaving all of it is preferable in emulation of the Prophet.
rows.anchor: والحلق أفضل من التقصير ولو حلق ربع الرأس يكتفى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Outside Hajj, the Prophet rarely shaved and usually left his hair; ʿAli regularly shaved after hearing that there is ritual impurity beneath every hair.
rows.anchor: وكان علي رضي الله عنه يحلق رأسه منذ ما سمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle من may be conditional or relative; مريضا is the predicate of كان, while منكم is a circumstantial phrase originally describing it.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون شرطية وموصولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The head ailment includes pain from a wound, lice, headache, or migraine; the pilgrim otherwise remains consecrated without shaving until sacrifice.
rows.anchor: كجراحة أو قمل أو صداع أو شقيقة

words: ففدية من صيام أو صدقة أو نسك
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Necessity permits shaving with a choice of three days' fasting, charity to six poor people at half a ṣāʿ of wheat each, or an animal sacrifice; a camel is best, then cow, then sheep.
rows.anchor: أي : صيام ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nusuk is the plural of nasīka, meaning a sacrificial animal; the three alternatives are expressed with أو for choice.
rows.anchor: أعلاها بدنة وأوسطها بقرة وأدناها شاة وأو للتخيير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Security means that fear has ended, illness has healed, and one is safe and at ease rather than under siege.
rows.anchor: من خوفكم وبرئتم من مرضكم وكنتم في حال أمن وسعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamattuʿ is either drawing near to God through ʿumra before Hajj in its months, or enjoying the permissions after ʿumra until entering Hajj consecration.
rows.anchor: فمن انتفع بالتقرب إلى الله تعالى بالعمرة قبل الانتفاع

rows.speaker: أبو يوسف
rows.claim: Abū al-Qāsim al-Ḥakīm used a sultan's gifts to repay debts after borrowing for his needs; Abū Yūsuf said this was permissible in such a case.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي يوسف قال هذا جواب أبيح في مثل هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To be impressed is to find something pleasing, incline toward it, and esteem it; al-Rāghib describes wonder as perplexity at not knowing a thing's cause.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب التعجب حيرة تعرض للإنسان عند الجهل بسبب الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading links the phrase to the speech: the person pleases you by what he says about worldly life, seeking worldly advantage rather than the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: متعلق بالقول أي : يسرك ما يقوله في معنى الدنيا وحقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, his eloquence and sweetness impress people in this world, but his falsehood and ugliness will become apparent in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: أو يعجبك قوله في الدنيا بحلاوته وفصاحته لا في الآخرة

words: ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says that God witnesses the love and Islam in his heart to agree with what his tongue professes.
rows.anchor: يقول الله شاهد أن ما في قلبي من المحبة والإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is the most intense adversary in hostility and disputes against Muslims; لدد means severity in disputation, and خصام is a verbal noun like قتال and جدال, with ألد added in the sense of 'in'.
rows.anchor: أشد في العداوة والخصومة للمسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about al-Akh nas ibn Shurayq al-Thaqafī, handsome and eloquent, who professed alliance, Islam, love, and sincerity toward the Prophet.
rows.anchor: نزلت في الأخنس بن شريف الثقفي

words: ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Claiming love and sincerity without matching heart and tongue is the conduct of heretics and hypocrites; a lover acts only as the beloved loves.
rows.anchor: والمحب لا يفعل إلا ما يحب محبوبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic verse and a couplet by Ḥāfiẓ illustrate that professed love is contradicted by disobedient deeds and falsehood; the true lover obeys the beloved.
rows.anchor: تعصي الإله وأنت تظهر حبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawallā may mean turning away from the Prophet's assembly or gaining dominance and becoming a ruler.
rows.anchor: أي : أدبر وانصرف عن مجلسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʿy is brisk walking, and by extension energetic effort in work or earning; saying 'in the earth' signals extensive corruption wherever he goes, since the encompassing setting implies encompassing action.
rows.anchor: السعي سير سريع بالأقدام وقد يستعار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihlāk means wasting or destroying; ḥarth is crops, and nasl is offspring of animal species, with both verbal nouns used here for what is produced.
rows.anchor: ما خرج من كل أنثى من أجناس الحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'to corrupt therein' gives the purpose of his striving.
rows.anchor: {ليفسد فيها} علة لسعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destruction may recall al-Akhnas's night attack on Thaqīf, which ruined their livestock and crops out of enmity, or the killings, dispossession, and oppression of corrupt governors.
rows.anchor: وذلك كما فعله الأخنس بثقيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says God placed blessing in crops and offspring when creating the means of subsistence, making their destruction the height of corruption.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "لما خلق الله تعالى أسباب المعيشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report describes a governor brought to judgment and cast on Hell's bridge: the obedient pass, while the disobedient break it and fall into Hell, a journey of fifty years.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "يجاء بالوالي يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God disapproves of corruption, hates it, and is angry with whoever engages in it.
rows.anchor: أي : لا يرتضيه ويبغضه ويغضب على من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's creating things is not corruption: corruption is removing something from a praiseworthy state without sound purpose; what seems corrupt from our perspective is, in the divine view, wholly right and good.
rows.anchor: وما نراه من فعله ونظنه بظاهره فسادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person addressed is the hypocrite and corrupter, being admonished and counseled.
rows.anchor: أي : لهذا المنافق والمفسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The admonition means to fear God in one's wrongdoing and abandon the corruption and hypocrisy one is practicing.
rows.anchor: خف من الله في صنعك السوء واترك ما تباشره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His arrogance or pre-Islamic zeal drives him into sin, or makes him reject the preacher's advice from stubbornness; the باء marks causation, from the idiom 'he made him do X'.
rows.anchor: حملته الأنفة التي فيها وحميته الجاهلية على الإثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell and lasting entry there suffice as recompense for what he has done; this is a severe threat.
rows.anchor: أي : كافيه دخول النار والخلود فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase swears that Hell is a wretched bed.
rows.anchor: أي : والله لبئس الفراش جهنم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd calls it among God's greatest sins for a servant told to fear God to retort, 'Worry about yourself.'
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه من أكبر الذنب

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: When ʿUmar was told to fear God, he put his cheek on the ground in humility.
rows.anchor: وقيل لعمر بن الخطاب رضي الله تعالى عنه اتقق الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing one who sacrifices religion for worldly gain, the next verse describes one who gives up worldly life and self for religion and God's reward in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: من يبذل دنياه ونفسه لطلب الدين وما عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To sell one's self means to devote it in worship for God's pleasure; the servant is figuratively seller and God buyer, exchanging the servant's devotion for divine reward and favor, although self and wealth already belong to God.
rows.anchor: لما بذل نفسه في طاعة الله من الصوم والصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here يشرى means 'sells,' although the exchange is described as a purchase: the emigrant bought himself free of the polytheists by surrendering his property.
rows.anchor: فيشري حينئذ بمعنى يشتري لجريان الحال على صورة الشراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was said to concern Ṣuhayb ibn Sinān al-Rūmī: pursued while emigrating from Mecca, he offered the Quraysh his property in exchange for release; Abū Bakr welcomed his profitable bargain, and Ṣuhayb rejoiced at the revelation.
rows.anchor: نزلت في صهيب بن سنان الرومي

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الشيرازي
rows.claim: In a dream, the Prophet warned that one who knows and follows a path to God but then turns back will suffer a punishment unmatched among the worlds; the report is cited from Lawaqiḥ al-Anwār al-Qudsiyya.
rows.anchor: قال أوحد المشايخ في وقته أبو عبد الله الشيرازي رأيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divorced women intended are free women who menstruate and whose marriages were consummated; nonconsummated women have no waiting period, pregnant or nonmenstruating women count by months or childbirth, and an enslaved woman's period is two cycles or two months.
rows.anchor: المراد بها ذوات الأقراء من الحرائر المدخول بهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root sense of divorce is to remove a bond; the women are those released from their husbands' bonds.
rows.anchor: رفع القيد أي : المخليات من حبال أزواجهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declarative form functions as a command: they are to wait.
rows.anchor: خبر في معنى الأمر أي : ليتربصن وينتظرن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The باء is causative: they make themselves wait and keep themselves in a waiting state.
rows.anchor: الباء للتعدية أي : يحملن أنفسهن على التربص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three cycles is accusative as a duration, meaning the period of three quruʾ, during which they may not marry.
rows.anchor: نصب على الظرفية أي : مدة ثلاثة قروء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quruʾ, plural of qarʾ, is an Arabic word with opposite senses, both purity and menstruation, like shafaq for redness and whiteness.
rows.anchor: والقروء جمع قرء وهو من الأضداد في كلام العرب

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and his companions take quruʾ as menstruations: since months replace cycles when menstruation ceases, menstruation must be the original measure.
rows.anchor: ذهب أبو حنيفة وأصحابه إلى أن القروء وهي الحيض

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī argues quruʾ means periods of purity, reading the timing phrase in 65:1 to rule out menstruation as the time for divorce.
rows.anchor: وتمسك الشافعي بقوله تعالى : {فطلقوهن لعدتهن}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers al-Shāfiʿī that the command means to divorce women facing their three menstrual periods; divorce comes first and the waiting period begins afterward.
rows.anchor: وجوابه أن معناه فطلقوهن مستقبلات لعدتهن وهي الحيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disagreement changes the waiting period: al-Shāfiʿī's is shorter, while Abū Ḥanīfa's is longer; for the latter, the remaining purity counts and the period ends only after the relevant menstruation finishes.
rows.anchor: وفائدة الخلاف بين الشافعي وأبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They must not conceal pregnancy or menstruation, for doing so could deny the husband's child or revocation rights, hasten separation, or lead to abortion; a woman might hide menstruation to secure a divorce during purity.
rows.anchor: من الحبل والحيض بأن تقول المرأة لست بحامل

words: ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports accepting women's statements about pregnancy or menstruation, whether affirming or denying them.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على قبول قولهن في ذلك نفيا وإثباتا

words: إن كن يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief in God and the Last Day, when punishment follows, should prevent concealment; the warning is severe, but the prohibition applies equally to believing and unbelieving women.
rows.anchor: فإن قضية الإيمان بالله واليوم الاخر الذي يقع فيه الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿl originally means lord or owner; a husband is called baʿl because he manages his wife, while baʿūla is a feminine collective plural, with tāʾ marking its collective femininity.
rows.anchor: وأصل البعل السيد والمالك سمي الزوج بعلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling a man baʿl after an explicit divorce signals that the marriage bond and permissibility remain; this concerns revocably divorced women, not irrevocably divorced women whose husbands lack return rights.
rows.anchor: ودلت تسمية الزوج بعلا بعد طلاقها الصريح على أن النكاح قائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A husband's right to return his wife to marriage exists only during the waiting period and ends when it expires.
rows.anchor: فإن حق الرجعة إنما يثبت للزوج ما دامت في العدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥaqq here means 'rightful' rather than comparative: outsiders have no right to the women, and a wife's refusal does not invalidate her husband's return.
rows.anchor: وأفعل هنا بمعنى الفاعل والمعنى أن أزواجهن حقيقون بردهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Husbands should return wives to reconcile and treat them well, not to harm them; the intention is exhortation and a warning against abuse, not a condition for a legally valid return.
rows.anchor: {إصلاحا} لما بينهم وبينهن وإحسانا إليهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In pre-Islamic practice, a man might return a wife near the end of her waiting period and divorce her again later to prolong it and harm her.
rows.anchor: كان الرجل يطلق امرأته فإذا قرب انقضاء عدتها راجعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing that return should benefit a wife, the verse sets out reciprocal rights between spouses.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى لما بين أن المقصود من الرجعة إصلاح حالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each spouse owes the other rights recognized by religious law and custom; equivalence means equal binding force and claim, not identical kinds of rights—for example, a husband owes dowry, maintenance, and housing.
rows.anchor: وجه المماثلة بين الحقين هو الوجوب واستحقاق المطالبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Men have an added degree of rights and merit over women, including differences in reason and religion; here the relevant superiority has two aspects.
rows.anchor: زيادة في الحق وفضل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First, the husband's rights are greater: he may divorce and revoke during the waiting period, while his wife owes obedience and cannot fast voluntarily or leave home without his permission; her rights include dowry, support, and freedom from harm.
rows.anchor: لا تصوم تطوعا إلا بإذنه ولا تخرج من بيتها إلا بإذنه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says both spouses receive the same marital pleasures, while the man's added merit is the care and financial duties he assumes for her.
rows.anchor: ما أشار إليه الزجاج بقوله معناه أن المرأة تنال من الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The degree can mean the husband's compassionate responsibilities: dowry, maintenance, housing, protection, care for her interests, and shielding her from harm.
rows.anchor: فالفضيلة على هذا فضيلة ما التزمه في حقها

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that, were prostration to a person permitted, he would command a wife to prostrate to her husband because God magnified his right over her.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse links to 4:34, where men's guardianship is tied to divine favor and their spending; the added duties make a wife's service in the home more emphatically obligatory.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى : {الرجال قوامون على النسآء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty to punish those who violate His rules, and wise: His laws contain wisdom and benefits.
rows.anchor: يقدر على الانتقام ممن يخالف أحكامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marriage succeeds when both spouses honor each other's rights and improve their shared life through children, upbringing, kind treatment, home care, and household management.
rows.anchor: مقاصد الزوجية لا تتم إلا إذا كان كل واحد من الزوجين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report calls a woman's good service to her husband her jihad.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "جهاد المرأة حسن التبعل"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that a woman who dies while her husband is pleased with her enters Paradise; it is cited in Riyāḍ al-Ṣāliḥīn.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "أيما امرأة ماتت وزوجها راضض عنها دخلت الجنة"

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says he adorns himself for his wife just as she adorns herself for him, treating adornment as a mutual right.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أني لأتزين لامرأتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A saying compares a woman to a dove that flies once its wings grow, warning that a husband who dresses his wife may find her unwilling to stay home.
rows.anchor: أن المرأة مثل الحمامة إذا نبت لها جناح طارت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anecdote has a man boast that no evil entered his house; a sage asks how his wife entered it.
rows.anchor: وقال رجل ما دخل داري شر قط فقال حكيم

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Al-Saʿdī's couplet praises a good woman as a source of comfort and asks God for protection from a bad woman.
rows.anchor: قال السعدي قدس سره :

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An unattributed couplet says a woman's chastity lies in her beauty and that display is forbidden unless lawful.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : عصمت زن را بمقام جمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pious Israelite's wife asked to become the most beautiful woman, then left him for rulers; his prayer turned her into a monkey, and his final prayer restored her, wasting all three granted requests.
rows.anchor: حكي أنه كان في بني إسرائيل رجل صالح وكان له امرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waiting period of divorced women symbolizes God's patience with servants who sever their bond: He delays turning away, allowing time for heedlessness to lift, love to stir, and repentance and return to arise.
rows.anchor: والإشارة أن المطلقات لما أمرن بالعدة وفاء لحق الصحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine grace calls the repentant seeker to leave the self and come back, and urges anyone seeking success to remain at God's threshold continually.
rows.anchor: فيقال من كمال الفضل والنوال يا قارع الباب دع نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion concerns the revocable divorce just mentioned in 2:228.
rows.anchor: أي : التطليق الرجعي المتقدم ذكره الذي قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Twice' means on two separate occasions, as giving two coins at once is not giving them twice; Abū Ḥanīfa deems combining two or three divorces in one act forbidden but effective.
rows.anchor: أي : دفعتان وذلك لا يكون إلا على سبيل التفريق

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa holds that a husband may revoke after only the first or second divorce; after three he has no return right, and she is unlawful until another marriage.
rows.anchor: فالطلاق الذي يثبت فيه للزوج حق المراجعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though declarative in form, the phrase commands divorce in two installments; a literal prediction could be contradicted by a combined divorce, which cannot be attributed to God's speech.
rows.anchor: وإن كان ظاهره الخبر فإن معناه الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After two divorces, either retain her through a proper, non-harmful return and good treatment or release her kindly by not returning before the waiting period ends.
rows.anchor: أي : فالحكم بعد هاتين الطلقتين إمساك لهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kind release includes paying her financial rights, not speaking ill of her after separation, and not turning people against her.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الإحسان في التسريح أنه إذا تركها أدى إليها حقوقها المالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After consummation, one or two divorces are revocable during the waiting period without her consent; after it expires, before consummation, or after khulʿ, remarriage requires a new contract and her consent and guardian's consent; after three divorces, another husband is required.
rows.anchor: إذا طلق زوجته طلقة أو طلقتين بعد الدخول بها يجوز له أن يراجعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For an enslaved man married to an enslaved woman, two divorces bar her until another marriage; Abū Ḥanīfa counts divorces by the woman, giving an enslaved man three against a free wife but a free man only two against an enslaved wife.
rows.anchor: وأما العبد إذا كانت تحته أمة فطلقها طلقتين فإنها لا تحل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear means fear of an enemy or another danger; رجالاً is an accusative circumstantial plural of راجل, with an omitted verb understood as 'pray walking'; ركبانا means mounted riders.
rows.anchor: منصوب على الحال وعامله محذوف تقديره فصلوا راجلين

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa holds that one must stop if possible: prayer while walking and fighting is not performed until stopping becomes possible, when one prays standing.
rows.anchor: ومذهب أبي حنيفة أنهم لا يصلون في حال المشي والمسايفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When danger is gone, 'remember God' means perform the normal prayer, whose most important pillar is remembrance.
rows.anchor: وزال خوفكم {فاذكروا الله} أي : فصلوا صلاة الأمن

words: كما علمكم ما لم تكونوا تعلمون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison means prayer should accord with God's teaching about its form; alternatively, give thanks in proportion to His teaching of previously unknown laws, including prayer in fear and safety.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالتشبيه أن تكون الصلاة المؤداة موافقة لما علمه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is a banquet prepared for monotheists five times each day; its varied pillars and actions are like dishes, each bringing pleasure and atonement for sins.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الصلاة بمنزلة الضيافة قد هيأها الله للموحدين

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Kaʿb al-Aḥbār relates God's words to Moses: noon prayer brings forgiveness, heavier scales, angelic intercession, and heaven's opening; for afternoon, requests are granted; sunset opens heaven; night prayer is better than the world and leaves worshippers like newborns.
rows.anchor: وعن كعب الأحبار أنه قال : قال الله لموسى

words: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening clause is God's own statement, not part of the believers' prayer.
rows.anchor: إخبار من الله تعالى وليس من كلام المؤمنين

words: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After 2:284 alarmed the Companions, they knelt before the Prophet, fearing they could not bear accounting for inner thoughts. He warned against answering like earlier scriptural communities; they affirmed obedience and sought forgiveness. After 2:285 was revealed, 2:286 eased the burden: the account concerns deliberate resolve to do evil, not unavoidable passing thoughts.
rows.anchor: روي أنه لما نزل قوله تعالى

words: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taklīf imposes a burden; wusʿ is what a person can accommodate without hardship. God, through favor and mercy to this community, assigns only what fits their capacity, as in 2:185.
rows.anchor: والوسع ما يسع الإنسان ولا يضيق عليه

words: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This shows that God has not actually imposed an impossible burden, not that such imposition is intrinsically impossible: its occurrence would make God's statement false, while an unrestricted negation does not establish impossibility.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على عدم وقوع التكليف بالمحال لا على امتناعه

words: لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul alone receives the reward for all the good it has earned and bears the punishment for all the evil it has acquired; no one else independently shares either account.
rows.anchor: من الخير الذي كلفت فعله لا لغيرها استقلالا أو اشتراكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses the more effortful form اكتسبت for evil because the desired act involves striving, unlike good; the iftiʿāl form conveys exertion.
rows.anchor: وإيراد الاكتساب في جانب الشر لأن الشر فيه اعتمال
